Software Stock Pullback Signaling Bulls to Move In
Liliana Orozco
Thu, October 15, 2026 at 11:09 AM PDT 1 min read
NET
Trade NET on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Shares of Cloudflare Inc (NYSE:NET) are down 4.6% to trade at $309.35, pacing for a fourth-straight losing session amid broader tech weakness. The shares are extending a pullback from their Oct. 6 all-time high of $370, which have brought them down to a historically bullish trendline. Year to date, the stock is up 57.4%.

Per Schaeffer's Senior Quantitative Analyst Rocky White, NET has traded within 0.75 times the 50-day moving average's 20-day average true range (ATR), after spending at least 80% of the previous two weeks above the trendline. This setup has occurred 10 other times over the last decade, after which the stock was higher one month later 70% of the time, averaging an 9.5% gain.

NET Chart 1015

Options traders have been leaning bearish, too. NET's 50-day put/call volume ratio of 0.87 at the International Securities Exchange (ISE) and Cboe Options Exchange (CBOE) ranks in the 98th percentile of its annual range. So while calls still outnumber puts on an absolute basis, this elevated ratio suggests an unwinding of pessimism could provide additional tailwinds for the stock.

Furthermore, Cloudware stock's 14-day Relative Strength Index (RSI) of 28 sits in "oversold" territory, which typically precedes a short-term bounce.

title: NET vs. FTNT: Which Cybersecurity Stock Should You Buy Right Now?
detail:
NET vs. FTNT: Which Cybersecurity Stock Should You Buy Right Now?
Om Jaiswal
Wed, October 14, 2026 at 5:42 AM PDT 5 min read
FTNT
NET
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Cloudflare NET and Fortinet Inc. FTNT are well-known players in the cybersecurity domain. While Cloudflare provides a cloud-native platform spanning network security, application security and connectivity, Fortinet combines a variety of hardware and cloud-based security solutions.

Both NET and FTNT are riding key industry trends, driven by the mounting incidents of credential theft, remote desktop protocol breaches and social engineering-based strikes by malicious actors. However, from an investment perspective, one stock offers a more favorable outlook than the other right now. Let's break down their fundamentals, growth prospects, market challenges and valuation to determine which stock offers a more compelling investment case.

The Case for NET Stock

Cloudflare is seeing stronger demand for its SASE and Zero Trust offerings as companies look to adopt AI more securely. Management said the key reason big companies are approaching Cloudflare is that they know they need AI but want to deploy it securely. This is creating new opportunities for the company's SASE and Zero Trust platforms, particularly as enterprises need to secure AI agents in addition to human users.

Cloudflare believes its developer-focused approach gives it an advantage in this market. Management said companies will have more AI agents working across their organizations and will need a security model designed for these agents. In one example, a large U.K. government agency was evaluating a first-generation Zero Trust provider but reconsidered the project after discussing its plans for AI agents with Cloudflare. Management said the agency canceled its existing request for proposal and is now reevaluating the project with an agents-first approach. Cloudflare believes its developer-focused approach has helped its SASE and Zero Trust platforms gain significant share over the past six months.

However, Cloudflare's non-GAAP gross margin was 73.1% in the second quarter of 2026, down 320 basis points from 76.3% a year ago. The main issue is the changing mix of traffic on Cloudflare's network. As paid traffic grows relative to free traffic, a larger portion of Cloudflare's network costs is being allocated to cost of revenue. This shows that Cloudflare is handling more traffic that requires infrastructure and network resources, putting pressure on gross margins.

This is particularly relevant as AI workloads and machine-to-machine traffic expand. These workloads can drive more usage and revenues, but they also require Cloudflare to provide more compute, network and storage capacity. Although management expects gross-margin pressure to stabilize, continued growth in AI and developer workloads could require higher infrastructure spending. This could limit near-term margin expansion even as revenues continue to grow rapidly.

title: What Was Cloudflare Telling You Before Its Stock Ran?
detail:
What Was Cloudflare Telling You Before Its Stock Ran?
Trefis Team

NET
AKAM
ZS
PANW
FTNT
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Image from Pixabay

Cloudflare (NET) stock returned 58.8% over the twelve months to October 12, 2026. During its August 2026 call, management credited growth to a more productive sales force alongside AI agent workloads on its network and its Workers developer platform. Neither theme was new by then. How early did Cloudflare start talking about them?

Cloudflare Named AI Before Its Revenue Showed It

Executives raised both themes well before October 9, 2025, the first day of the twelve months measured here. During the November 7, 2024 call, the company described Cloudflare as a single cloud platform for running AI models. It also noted the addition of a record number of new large customers.

The February 6, 2025 call offered an even clearer message. "The killer application for Cloudflare Workers is turning out to be AI," management said. The company noted that sales productivity had risen from a year earlier for a fifth straight quarter. At the same time, it pointed out that the capacity of its sales force had been holding the business back.

Official figures took longer to reflect these themes. Revenue grew 27.8% in the second quarter of 2025, the newest quarter filed before that October date, compared to 30.0% a year earlier. Investors could hear the case from management before they could see it in revenue.

The stock rose before revenue growth did. The shares were down 39% from their mid-February high by April 18, 2025. Yet they rose 109.4% over the six months before October 9, 2025. The stock was already climbing when the measured twelve months began.

Cloudflare's Sales Then Caught Up With Its Words

The stock outperformed the broader market over those twelve months, a period when the S&P 500 returned 17.3%. Cloudflare's competitors did not move in tandem: Palo Alto Networks returned 87.7% during the window, while Zscaler lost 28.4%.

Cloudflare's reported revenue caught up over the same twelve months. It rose 36% from a year earlier in the second quarter of 2026, compared to 27.8% in the same quarter of 2025.

Existing customers were spending more as well. Dollar-based net retention, which tracks spending by existing clients against a year earlier, stood at 120% on the August 6, 2026 call. Management had reported a figure of 110% during the November 2024 call. The company also noted in August that Workers had become a meaningful contributor to revenue, though Cloudflare does not report revenue by product.

Cloudflare Guided For A Smaller Sales Gain

Executives guided for revenue growth of 31% in the third quarter of 2026, compared to the 36% reported for the second quarter. The third quarter has ended, but its results are not yet out. Management said its business is moving toward usage-based contracts, making quarter-to-quarter results harder to forecast. It sets guidance prudently for this reason.

Cloudflare (NET) closed the most recent trading day at $350.87, moving -2.79% from the previous trading session. This change lagged the S&P 500's 0.06% loss on the day. At the same time, the Dow added 0.38%, and the tech-heavy Nasdaq lost 0.44%.

Heading into today, shares of the web security and content delivery company had gained 17.75% over the past month, outpacing the Computer and Technology sector's gain of 4.85% and the S&P 500's gain of 2.36%.

The investment community will be paying close attention to the earnings performance of Cloudflare in its upcoming release. The company's earnings per share (EPS) are projected to be $0.35, reflecting a 29.63% increase from the same quarter last year. At the same time, our most recent consensus estimate is projecting a revenue of $733.3 million, reflecting a 30.47% rise from the equivalent quarter last year.

For the full year, the Zacks Consensus Estimates project earnings of $1.26 per share and a revenue of $2.87 billion, demonstrating changes of +35.48% and +32.54%, respectively, from the preceding year.

Investors might also notice recent changes to analyst estimates for Cloudflare. These latest adjustments often mirror the shifting dynamics of short-term business patterns. Therefore, positive revisions in estimates convey analysts' confidence in the business performance and profit potential.

Research indicates that these estimate revisions are directly correlated with near-term share price momentum. Investors can capitalize on this by using the Zacks Rank. This model considers these estimate changes and provides a simple, actionable rating system.

The Zacks Rank system, ranging from #1 (Strong Buy) to #5 (Strong Sell), possesses a remarkable history of outdoing, externally audited, with #1 stocks returning an average annual gain of +25% since 1988. Within the past 30 days, our consensus EPS projection remained stagnant. At present, Cloudflare boasts a Zacks Rank of #3 (Hold).

Looking at valuation, Cloudflare is presently trading at a Forward P/E ratio of 285.51. This signifies a premium in comparison to the average Forward P/E of 20.96 for its industry.

Meanwhile, NET's PEG ratio is currently 7.64. The PEG ratio is similar to the widely-used P/E ratio, but this metric also takes the company's expected earnings growth rate into account. The average PEG ratio for the Internet - Software industry stood at 1.21 at the close of the market yesterday.

The Internet - Software industry is part of the Computer and Technology sector. This group has a Zacks Industry Rank of 94, putting it in the top 39% of all 250+ industries.
